subject: number of SNPs input/output in userGWAS not matching

messages.author: 43bf2fdc8e90d845
messages.subject: number of SNPs input/output in userGWAS not matching
parts:
Hi All,

Wondering if anyone has come across the following issue, using the userGWAS function:

I have divided my userGWAS job into 40 different jobs by splitting the sumstats into separate data files. One of the sumstats files, for example, included 114,763 SNPs. The output file from userGWAS, however, only had 113,322 rows.

Any ideas on where these "missing" snps are? Although I haven't checked all of the output files, if we assume a similar number of SNPs are missing in each of the 40 output files, that would mean that ~60k SNPs are "missing" from the output. There are a total number of ~4.5mil SNPs in my sumstats files. So 60k missing is probably not a big deal for my purposes(?) - I am constructing PGSs without a p-value cut-off.

Any and all feedback would be much appreciated.

Thank you GenomicSEM creators!

Best,
Arianna

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: number of SNPs input/output in userGWAS not matching
parts:
Hi Arianna, 

Thanks for sending along those files! It turns out that there was a bug when using parallel processing within userGWAS where runs that did not converge were not being saved to the output. This has been corrected on the master branch if you want to re-download, restart R, and load the package. You will find that if you re-run the model for just those ~50K SNPs that were not present in the full output that you sent me that this returns NAs and warnings about the model not converging. It looks like if you use unit loading identification for these SNPs that the model more readily finds a solution and ends up converging for the handful of SNPs I've tested. As you likely know, switching over to this form of model identification would not require re-running the model for the other SNPs; the unstandardized point estimates and standard error for the SNP effect on the factor will change based on the form of identification used, but the ratio of estimate over standard error (i.e., z-statistic and corresponding p-value) will be maintained regardless of whether you use unit loading or unit variance identification. Code for running the leftover SNPs with the model I'm suggesting is directly below. Thanks for brining this to my attention and let me know if you run into any more issues!

Best, 
  Andrew  

sumstats<-fread("sumstats.txt",data.table=FALSE)
data<-read.csv("onefactor_fullresults_041520.csv")
#pull out subset of SNPs that were not previously saved
Left<-subset(sumstats, !(sumstats$SNP %in% data$SNP))

#specify model using unit loading ID
#note that lavaan will automatically fix the loading of the first factor indicator unless told otherwise
onefactor_loadingID<-"F1=~AB + ADHD + CANNABIS + ALCDEP + ANXIETY + MDD + NEUROT
F1~SNP"

Leftovers<-userGWAS(covstruc = LDSC_intext,SNPs=Left,model=onefactor_loadingID,sub=c("F1~SNP"), modelchi=TRUE)
